newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Ericsson says sells radio system to Russia.
newsitem.headline: Ericsson says sells radio system to Russia.

text.p: Swedish telecoms firm LM Ericsson AB said on Tuesday it had sold a radio system to the city of Moscow for radio coverage of the Russian capital and surrounding area.

The system, EDACS (Enhanced Digital Access Communications System), is a private radio system that is designed for use by the police, fire brigade, rescue services, airports and industrial companies, Ericsson said in a statement.
EDACS handles both voice and data communications at the same time.

The system will be supplied by Ericsson after signing a contract with the Russian telecoms holding company AO Rosiko, a Russian holding company set up in 1995 as a system integrator for telecommunication projects.
Installation will begin in mid-October and the first radio base stations would be working by December 1997, Ericsson said.
Ericsson said the Russian Federation Federal Guard Service had been equipped with the system since 1994.
